rules: every substantive claim is claim-local and must preserve population intervention comparator outcome evidence class jurisdiction source ids and snapshot ids
a guideline recommendation is not individualized medical advice
a positive trial or meta-analysis result is not a cure claim
aggregate CBT evidence must not be silently inherited by a different protocol delivery format population or condition
archived guidance remains historical evidence and must not be relabelled as current guidance
stale verification means review is due; it does not mean the underlying claim is automatically false

claims.population: Adults in England with a new episode of less severe depression.
claims.intervention: Group cognitive behavioural therapy delivered in line with current treatment manuals by appropriately trained practitioners.
claims.comparator: Other first-line options listed by NICE; this record does not assert that group CBT is superior to them.
claims.outcome: Status as a first-line treatment option within shared decision-making.
claims.claim_text: NICE lists group CBT among first-line treatment options for less severe depression and says treatment choice should be matched to clinical needs and preferences through shared decision-making.
not_established: Group CBT is not established here as the best option for every person.
A guideline recommendation is not individualized medical advice or a cure claim.

claims.population: Adults in England with a new episode of more severe depression.
claims.intervention: Individual cognitive behavioural therapy delivered by a practitioner with therapy-specific training and competence.
claims.comparator: Other first-line options in NICE guidance, including combined psychological treatment and medication options.
claims.outcome: Status as a first-line treatment option within shared decision-making.
claims.claim_text: NICE includes individual CBT among first-line treatment options for more severe depression and requires treatment choice to be matched to clinical needs and preferences.
not_established: This does not establish superiority over every other first-line option.
This does not authorize an AI to select treatment for an individual.

claims.population: Adults in England with diagnosed GAD whose symptoms have not improved after education and active monitoring.
claims.intervention: Non-facilitated self-help, guided self-help, or psychoeducational groups based on CBT principles as specified by NICE.
claims.comparator: Other Step 2 low-intensity options; choice is guided by preference.
claims.outcome: Status as a first-line Step 2 intervention.
claims.claim_text: NICE recommends one or more low-intensity interventions at Step 2 for GAD and specifies that the self-help and psychoeducational options are based on CBT principles.
not_established: The repository's generic exercises are not automatically equivalent to the structured programmes specified by NICE.
This is not a diagnosis or individual treatment recommendation.

claims.population: Adults in England with GAD and marked functional impairment or an inadequate response to Step 2 interventions who choose a high-intensity psychological intervention.
claims.intervention: Individual high-intensity CBT based on clinical-trial treatment manuals and delivered by trained and competent practitioners.
claims.comparator: Applied relaxation is another high-intensity psychological option; drug treatment is also a Step 3 mode of treatment.
claims.outcome: Guideline recommendation to offer CBT or applied relaxation when high-intensity psychological treatment is chosen.
claims.claim_text: For Step 3 GAD, NICE says that if a person chooses a high-intensity psychological intervention, offer CBT or applied relaxation, and specifies trained and competent delivery for CBT.
not_established: The guideline does not make this repository a provider of high-intensity CBT.
The recommendation does not establish CBT as superior to drug treatment for every person.

claims.population: Adults aged 18 years or older with a primary diagnosis of GAD across 65 randomized clinical trials; 5048 participants contributed to the network meta-analysis.
claims.intervention: Cognitive behavioural therapy as represented in the included randomized trials.
claims.outcome: GAD symptom severity at post-treatment and at 3 to 12 months after treatment.
claims.claim_text: In the 2024 network meta-analysis, CBT was associated with lower GAD symptom severity than treatment as usual at post-treatment, and the association remained at 3 to 12 months.
not_established: The pooled result does not imply equal effectiveness across every CBT protocol or delivery format.
The pooled result does not predict an individual's response.

claims.population: 4361 participants with GAD across 52 randomized trials; mean age 43 years and 69.7% women.
claims.intervention: CBT analysed by delivery format, including individual, group and remote CBT.
claims.comparator: Other CBT delivery formats, treatment as usual, and waiting-list controls.
claims.claim_text: The 2025 delivery-format network meta-analysis found individual CBT superior to treatment as usual and waiting list for GAD symptoms, while remote CBT was not superior to treatment as usual or waiting list in that analysis.

remote_cbt_vs_treatment_as_usual.reported_result: not statistically superior in the network meta-analysis

not_established: This does not prove that every remote CBT programme is ineffective.
The sign convention differs from some other meta-analyses; do not combine estimates without checking outcome coding.

claims.population: 175 adult primary-care patients with PHQ-9 scores of 10 or greater in the randomized trial.
claims.intervention: Clinician-supported computer-assisted CBT using a nine-lesson program plus treatment as usual.
claims.outcome: PHQ-9 depressive symptom scores after 12 weeks and during follow-up.
claims.claim_text: In this randomized primary-care trial, clinician-supported computer-assisted CBT plus usual care produced greater improvement in PHQ-9 scores than usual care alone at post-treatment and follow-up.
not_established: This result is specific to the tested computer-assisted programme plus therapist support and usual care.
It does not establish the same effect for unguided self-help or the CBT 95 exercises.

claims.population: Participants with a formal diagnosis of depression in 62 independent randomized-trial samples published from 2019 through 2023.
claims.intervention: Classic and contemporary cognitive behavioural therapies represented in the included superiority trials.
claims.comparator: Control conditions used in the included superiority randomized controlled trials.
claims.outcome: Depressive symptom outcomes at post-treatment and follow-up.
claims.claim_text: The 2025 review of recent CBT randomized trials for formally diagnosed depression reported medium-to-large post-treatment effects across the included literature, with follow-up effects either maintained or reduced depending on the analysis.
not_established: The review was limited to formally diagnosed depression and superiority trials in its specified publication window.
An effect-size range is not an individual prognosis and does not establish cure.

claims.population: Members of the public using NHS Every Mind Matters self-help material.
claims.intervention: Self-help CBT techniques such as noticing thought-behaviour cycles, reframing and structured problem solving.
claims.comparator: None; this is an educational-material claim rather than an efficacy comparison.
claims.outcome: Availability and educational description of CBT-style self-help techniques.
claims.claim_text: NHS Every Mind Matters publishes self-help CBT techniques intended to help people understand and work with links among thoughts, feelings and behaviours.
not_established: Publication as self-help material does not by itself establish treatment efficacy for a particular condition.
Educational self-help is not automatically equivalent to clinician-delivered CBT.

claims.population: People with major depressive disorder within the scope of the 2020 RANZCP mood-disorders guideline.
claims.intervention: Cognitive behavioural therapy for acute depression.
claims.comparator: Other psychological treatments discussed in the historical guideline.
claims.outcome: Historical guideline prioritisation of CBT and interpersonal psychotherapy as primary recommended approaches.
claims.claim_text: The 2020 RANZCP mood-disorders guideline described CBT and interpersonal psychotherapy as primary recommended approaches for acute depression, but RANZCP now marks that guideline as more than five years old and no longer current guidance.
not_established: This historical guideline must not be represented as current Australian clinical guidance.
Historical priority language must not override current jurisdiction-specific guidance.
